hero.headline: US Strikes Iran Again as Fragile Ceasefire Frays
hero.body:
The United States conducted new military strikes against Iran on Wednesday, targeting attack drones and a drone ground control station in the country's south. A US official characterized the attacks as self-defense measures, marking the second round of American military action in three days.

The strikes occurred amid a month-old ceasefire that continues to show signs of instability. The military escalation threatens ongoing negotiations aimed at ending a three-month conflict between the two nations.

Iran responded to the American strikes by attacking a US airbase, according to Iranian claims. Oil prices jumped 3 percent following Iran's announcement, reflecting concerns about potential disruptions to global energy supplies.

The recent military actions complicate diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict. President Trump rejected Iran's counter-proposal to a US peace plan, calling it "totally unacceptable." The Iranian response, passed through Pakistani mediators, emphasized the necessity of lifting US sanctions, ending the American naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and guarantees against renewed attacks.

The US had presented a one-page, 14-point memorandum of understanding a week earlier. That proposal reportedly included a moratorium on Iranian nuclear enrichment lasting up to 20 years, the transfer of Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile overseas, and the dismantling of Iranian nuclear facilities.

Iran's counter-proposal suggested shorter timelines and more limited concessions. The country offered a shorter enrichment moratorium, partial export of enriched uranium, and refusal to accept facility dismantling.

Netanyahu warned that the war remains unfinished, stating that Iranian nuclear stockpiles must be removed. "It's not over, because there's still nuclear material that has to be taken out of Iran," Netanyahu told CBS, adding that the best approach would involve entering Iran to secure the fissile material as part of an agreement.

Trump indicated he had discussed potential military options with Netanyahu. He stated the US could "go in for two more weeks and do every single target," though he noted that remaining targets would constitute "final touches" to operations already underway.

The ceasefire, declared on April 8, showed renewed strain as the UAE and Kuwait reported drone incursions in their airspace. A drone attack also started a small fire on a ship off the coast in the region.

Trump downplayed some concerns about Iran's enriched uranium stockpile, suggesting that satellite surveillance through the Space Force was sufficient to monitor access. He expressed confidence that "if anybody got near the place, we will know about it and we'll blow them up."

The situation has created significant uncertainty in energy markets and raised concerns about further escalation. Trump faces pressure to maintain the ceasefire ahead of a scheduled visit to China, which has been pushing for an end to hostilities and the opening of the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: At least 2 dead, 9 missing after chemical tank implosion at Washington state paper mill
cards.body:
At least two people are dead and nine workers remain unrecovered after a chemical tank implosion at a paper mill in Longview, Washington.

The disaster involved white liquor, a caustic chemical used in paper production. Contaminated water from the implosion is being flushed through Longview's ditch system as part of the response effort.

Washington's governor said the incident could be the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history. The statement underscores the severity of the accident at the facility.

Emergency responders are working to locate the nine workers who remain unaccounted for. The implosion occurred at a tank containing the chemical solution, which is part of the paper manufacturing process.

White liquor is a mixture of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide dissolved in water. The substance is highly alkaline and used to break down wood chips into pulp during papermaking. Contact with the chemical can cause severe burns and other injuries.

Authorities have not disclosed what caused the tank to implode or the full extent of injuries to workers at the scene. The paper mill is a major employer in the Longview area.

The contaminated water cleanup effort involves directing the chemical-laden runoff through existing drainage infrastructure. Officials have not provided details on environmental impacts or risks to nearby waterways.

Search and recovery operations continue for the nine missing workers. The two confirmed deaths add to what is already one of the most serious workplace accidents in recent Washington state history.

The facility remains closed as investigators work to determine the cause of the implosion and assess damage to the tank and surrounding structures.

cards.headline: U.S. conducts second strike on Iran in three days
cards.teaser: American forces hit a drone launch site in Iran as negotiations to end the three-month conflict continue.
cards.body:
The United States conducted defensive strikes against an Iranian military facility after downing Iranian attack drones, according to U.S. officials. This marks the second American military action against Iran in three days.

The strikes occur amid a fragile ceasefire and ongoing negotiations to end the three-month conflict between the two nations. President Trump continues to maintain maximum demands on Iran as talks remain stalled. Oil prices have risen following the military action amid concerns about potential disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone site as negotiations continue
cards.body:
The US military struck an Iranian ground control station and shot down four Iranian drones over the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to US Central Command and a senior official.

US forces intercepted four Iranian one-way attack drones that posed a threat to a commercial ship in the strait. The military then struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas, a port city on Iran's southern coast, that was preparing to launch a fifth drone, a US official told reporters on condition of anonymity.

This marks the second military clash between US and Iranian forces in 48 hours, even as the two countries are negotiating an agreement to end their conflict. The escalation occurred while diplomatic talks aimed at resolving the broader war continue.

President Trump addressed the Iran situation during a Cabinet meeting Wednesday, where his remarks differed from statements he made over the weekend suggesting an agreement was close. Trump held to what officials described as maximum demands on Iran during the meeting.

The commercial vessel targeted by the Iranian drones was in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway through which significant global oil shipments pass. US Central Command confirmed its forces shot down the Iranian drones but did not provide additional details about the commercial ship or potential damage.

The Iranian military had fired the four one-way drones at the ship before US intervention, the senior official said. The ground station strike in Bandar Abbas was intended to prevent the launch of additional drones.

The incident highlights ongoing tensions between Washington and Tehran despite active diplomatic efforts. US and Iranian negotiators have been working toward a deal to end the conflict, though the timing and terms of any agreement remain uncertain following these latest military actions.

cards.headline: Israel Orders Mass Evacuations in Southern Lebanon as Fighting Intensifies
cards.teaser: Israeli military told residents of large areas of southern Lebanon to leave their homes.
cards.body:
Israel has declared large areas of southern Lebanon south of the Zahrani River as "combat zones" and issued evacuation orders for residents. The military has threatened fresh strikes against Hezbollah as fighting intensifies in the region.

The escalation marks a significant expansion of the conflict in southern Lebanon, with Israeli forces intensifying operations against the militant group.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo Over Ebola Outbreak
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola cases spread.
cards.body:
Uganda has closed its border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo following an Ebola outbreak in the region. Seven confirmed cases have been reported in Kampala, Uganda's capital, prompting the government to take preventive measures to contain the virus's spread.

The World Health Organization's director-general has called for an immediate ceasefire in eastern Congo, warning of a "catastrophic collision of disease and conflict" as the Ebola outbreak in Ituri province outpaces response efforts. Uganda's disease surveillance systems are being mobilized to manage the situation, while international airlines have been urged to implement safety protocols similar to those used during the COVID pandemic.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Prosecutors say the ex-agency official stole approximately 300 gold bars from the CIA.
cards.body:
Federal authorities arrested David Rush, a former CIA official, after discovering $40 million worth of gold bars in his home. The FBI executed the arrest following the discovery of the precious metals.

Prosecutors allege Rush stole the gold from the CIA during his time with the agency. Court documents indicate the former officer is accused of defrauding the government by lying about his credentials. Sources say approximately 300 gold bars were recovered from his residence. The case involves one of the largest thefts from a U.S. intelligence agency in recent memory.

cards.headline: Google Engineer Charged With Insider Trading on Polymarket Bets
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged a Google employee with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company information to make $1.2 million on prediction market bets.

The engineer, identified as Michele Spagnuolo, worked at Google and allegedly accessed nonpublic data about search trends through his position. He then used that information to place wagers on Polymarket, a platform where users bet on real-world events including political outcomes, economic indicators, and other measurable occurrences.

According to the unsealed complaint, Spagnuolo placed bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and risked more than $2.7 million on the wagers. Prosecutors say he knew the outcome of these bets before the general public because he had accessed Google's confidential information about search-related trends.

The charges represent a notable application of insider trading law to prediction markets. While insider trading statutes traditionally apply to securities markets, federal authorities argue the same legal principles extend to any market where nonpublic information provides an unfair advantage. The case marks only the second known instance of the federal government filing criminal charges against someone for allegedly using insider information to profit on a prediction market platform.

Search trend data represents particularly valuable information because it can reveal shifting public interest before it becomes widely known. Spagnuolo's access to Google's internal systems gave him an advantage unavailable to other bettors on Polymarket.

Prediction markets like Polymarket have grown in popularity as a forecasting tool based on collective predictions. Users can profit when their predictions prove correct. The platform has gained attention recently for allowing bets on various high-stakes events, raising concerns about potential misuse of classified or confidential information.

The $1.2 million in alleged profits suggests Spagnuolo made multiple successful bets over a period of time. Prosecutors have not disclosed which specific events or search trends the bets covered or the duration of the alleged scheme.

Insider trading charges carry potential prison sentences and substantial financial penalties. The defendant faces prosecution under federal laws designed to ensure fair markets by preventing individuals with privileged access to information from exploiting it for personal gain.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges. The company employs thousands of engineers who have access to various types of internal data as part of their regular work responsibilities. The case highlights the challenges companies face in monitoring employees' personal financial activities, particularly as prediction markets and cryptocurrency-based betting platforms continue to expand.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination from firefighting foam
cards.body:
The Australian government filed a lawsuit against American manufacturing giant 3M over contamination from chemicals used in firefighting foam at defense sites across the country. The case seeks A$2 billion in damages and represents the largest legal action ever brought by the Australian government.

The lawsuit centers on contamination caused by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly known as PFAS or forever chemicals, which were used in firefighting foam at military installations. These synthetic chemicals earned their nickname because they do not break down naturally in the environment and can persist for thousands of years.

3M, a multinational conglomerate headquartered in Minnesota, manufactured the firefighting foam products that contained these chemicals. The foam was widely used at defense facilities for its effectiveness in suppressing fuel fires.

PFAS chemicals have raised health and environmental concerns globally because they accumulate in soil, water, and human bodies over time. Scientists have linked exposure to these substances with various health problems, though the Australian government has not specified the extent of contamination at the affected defense sites or the number of locations involved.

The Australian legal action follows similar lawsuits against 3M in other countries. In the United States, 3M agreed to pay more than $10 billion to settle claims related to PFAS contamination of public water systems. The company also faced litigation over contamination at military bases and airports where the firefighting foam was used.

3M stopped manufacturing PFAS-based firefighting foam in 2002 and announced in 2022 that it would phase out all PFAS production by the end of 2025. However, the legacy contamination from decades of use remains a persistent problem at sites around the world.

The Australian case marks an escalation in government efforts to hold manufacturers accountable for environmental damage from forever chemicals. The A$2 billion figure reflects the scale of cleanup costs and potential remediation required at contaminated defense installations.

Neither 3M nor Australian government officials provided additional details about which specific defense sites are affected or the timeline for legal proceedings.

cards.headline: Crystal Palace win Conference League with Mateta goal against Rayo Vallecano
cards.body:
Crystal Palace secured their first European trophy after Jean-Philippe Mateta scored the decisive goal in their Conference League final victory over Rayo Vallecano in Leipzig. The triumph represents a historic moment for the club, which had never previously won a continental competition.

The win proved particularly significant given the circumstances surrounding it. Palace had been denied a place in this season's Europa League despite winning the FA Cup last year, after being judged to have breached European football's multi-club ownership rules. This Conference League success now grants them automatic qualification for next season's Europa League.

It was a fitting finale for manager Oliver Glasner, who departs after transforming the club's fortunes. The Austrian performed a full-length dive on the pitch in celebration before collecting his winners' medal. With this victory, Glasner has now won three trophies in 12 months, including last season's FA Cup and Community Shield.

Palace struggled in the opening half, with Rayo dominating possession and creating the better chances. The Spanish side, competing in their first final in 102 years, posed constant threats down their flanks. However, Glasner's tactical adjustments proved decisive after the interval.

The decisive moment came early in the second half when Mateta showed instinctive finishing to convert from close range after Adam Wharton's shot was parried by Rayo goalkeeper Augusto Batalla. The French striker's rebound finish sparked wild celebrations among Palace's supporters.

The match remained tense as Rayo pressed for an equalizer. Batalla was called upon to make crucial saves, while Palace's defence, anchored by Maxence Lacroix, held firm under sustained pressure. Rayo manager Iñigo Pérez used all his substitutes in attempting to breach Palace's resistance, but they could not find a way through.

Palace's chairman Steve Parish attended the match alongside Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, witnessing the club's greatest night since he rescued them from administration 16 years ago. The victory resonated deeply with the travelling support, with thousands of Palace fans gathering in Leipzig to witness the historic achievement.

Approximately 15,000 Palace supporters made the journey to Germany, replicating the marches that had preceded their FA Cup final appearance against Manchester City the previous year. Both sets of supporters displayed large tifos before kick-off, with Palace's banner referencing their remarkable journey from the brink of extinction to winning their first major trophy.

The Conference League triumph concludes an extraordinary period under Glasner's management and provides Palace with entry into Europe's second-tier competition for the coming season, elevating the club to the level where ambitions can now be properly realised.

cards.headline: Justice Department investigates Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Department of Justice opened a criminal investigation into whether Carroll committed perjury during deposition testimony in her civil case.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to reports from CNN and the New York Times on Wednesday.

Prosecutors are examining whether Carroll, 82, committed perjury during a 2022 deposition in her civil lawsuits against Trump. She testified at that time that she did not accept outside financial support for her legal battles.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan Continue Fighting Despite China Mediation Efforts
cards.teaser: Open warfare between Pakistan and Afghanistan has continued for months with no resolution in sight.
cards.body:
Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan months ago, and neither country appears ready to end hostilities. China has attempted to mediate between the two nations but has not succeeded in brokering peace.

The conflict has extended well beyond initial expectations. Both Pakistan and Afghanistan have maintained their military postures despite diplomatic pressure from regional powers to stand down.

cards.headline: China's Pork Prices Hit 16-Year Low as Consumer Spending Weakens
cards.teaser: Pork prices in China, a key inflation measure, reached their lowest level in 16 years.
cards.body:
Pork prices in China have fallen to their lowest level in 16 years, reflecting weak consumer demand and excessive hog production. As a key inflation indicator in China, the decline signals economic strain on households that are spending less.

The price drop underscores broader pressures in the Chinese economy, where consumers are tightening their budgets while hog farmers face oversupply challenges in the sector.

cards.headline: China Expands Factory Network Overseas as Trade Surplus Grows
cards.teaser: China is building manufacturing facilities around the world as its trade surplus continues to expand.
cards.body:
Chinese companies are establishing factories in countries across the globe, a move that has raised concerns among local competitors. The expansion comes as China's trade surplus has grown to $1.2 trillion.

The factory exports represent a shift in how China engages with global trade. Rather than only shipping finished goods, Chinese manufacturers are now setting up production facilities in foreign markets.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California civil rights agency won a legal victory against Tesla as the court denied the company's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination case.
cards.body:
A California court rejected Tesla's motion to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency. The ruling allows the case to proceed to trial, which is expected to begin in July.

The California Civil Rights Department celebrated the court's decision as a significant victory in its legal action against Tesla over allegations of racial discrimination at the company's facilities.

cards.headline: Hurricanes take 3-1 series lead over Canadiens with Andersen shutout
cards.teaser: Frederik Andersen stopped 18 shots for his third playoff shutout as Carolina moved within one win of the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
Frederik Andersen delivered a dominant performance in net for the Hurricanes, stopping 18 shots to earn his third shutout of the postseason. The shutout victory gave Carolina a 3-1 series advantage over Montreal in the Eastern Conference finals.

With the win, the Hurricanes moved one victory away from reaching the Stanley Cup Final.

cards.headline: Phillies pitcher Cristopher Sanchez breaks franchise scoreless innings record
cards.teaser: Sanchez extended his streak to 44 scoreless innings, surpassing a mark set by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander in 1911.
cards.body:
Cristopher Sánchez set a new Phillies franchise record on Wednesday, extending his scoreless innings streak to 44⅔ innings. The left-hander surpassed the previous mark held by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander, whose record had stood since 1911.

Sánchez's achievement represents one of the most impressive pitching performances in Philadelphia baseball history, breaking a franchise standard that had endured for more than a century.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to review Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges requested a court reopen Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges asked a federal court Wednesday to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argued the administration circumvented proper judicial oversight by negotiating a settlement directly with the president rather than through the courts.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare and weaponization." The former judges contend this arrangement bypassed necessary judicial review of the case.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged President Trump and members of Congress to provide Patriot missile interceptors to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and Congress on Wednesday to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. Zelensky said Ukraine has built strong defenses against drones but lacks domestic capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

Zelensky told lawmakers that while Ukraine achieved significant success defending against drones, it has not developed its own production of systems to counter missile attacks. He requested the interceptors as part of efforts to end the conflict with Russia.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Partial Internet Access After 88 Days of Near-Total Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government is allowing some people to reconnect with the world after months offline.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access after maintaining a near-total shutdown for 88 days that blocked television, chat services, and online news. The move comes as the country navigates a fragile ceasefire with the US during ongoing negotiations to end a three-month conflict.

The reconnection remains incomplete and uncertain. Not all Iranians have regained access, and those who have worry about how long the restored service will continue, given the government's track record of cutting communications.

cards.headline: Ferrari's First Electric Car Meets Resistance in Italy and Beyond
cards.teaser: Ferrari's debut electric vehicle faced criticism online and skepticism from analysts following its release.
cards.body:
Ferrari unveiled its new Luce electric model, prompting significant backlash. The vehicle sparked mockery on social media and divided public opinion, while investors responded by selling shares in the Italian automaker.

A former Ferrari chairman warned that the electric car could destroy the brand's legacy. The criticism reflects deeper concerns about whether an electric vehicle aligns with Ferrari's identity as a manufacturer of high-performance combustion engine sports cars.

cards.headline: Global Automakers Struggle to Match China's Electric Vehicle Dominance
cards.teaser: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers have built control over the supply chains shaping the global auto industry.
cards.body:
Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers have established dominant positions across the global automotive supply chain. The BBC's factory visits in China documented how domestic EV producers control critical segments of the industry, including battery production, raw materials processing, and manufacturing infrastructure that international automakers depend on for their own electric vehicle development.

This control over key ecosystem components gives Chinese producers a significant competitive advantage in shaping the future of the global auto industry.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 electric SUVs
cards.teaser: Electric vehicle maker Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of its R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe called it "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date."

The R2 marks Rivian's expansion into a more affordable segment of the electric SUV market, complementing its existing R1T truck and R1S SUV lineup.

cards.headline: Google's artificial intelligence struggles with basic spelling tasks
cards.teaser: Google's AI systems are having difficulty spelling common words, including the company's own name, in a persistent technical problem.
cards.body:
Google is facing criticism over spelling errors in its artificial intelligence systems. The company's AI has struggled to correctly spell common words, including "Google" itself, as well as instruction words like "disregard," "stop," and "ignore." These spelling failures have been widely reported across Google's AI search features and language models.

The issues come as Google has made AI-generated answers central to its search experience. This shift represents a significant change for SEO strategies that previously relied on traditional search results, with brands now having limited visibility into how Google's AI describes them to users.

cards.headline: SEC commissioner says conference still best despite Big Ten's recent dominance
cards.teaser: Greg Sankey defended the SEC's status even as the Big Ten has won three straight national titles and holds a 4-0 playoff record against SEC teams.
cards.body:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said his league "stands alone" and remains the best conference despite recent setbacks. The Big Ten has won three consecutive national championships and maintains a perfect 4-0 record against the SEC in head-to-head College Football Playoff matchups over the past three seasons.

Sankey made his comments during college football spring meetings as conference realignment discussions continue to dominate the sport's landscape.

cards.headline: Georgia coach suggests SEC could leave NCAA without College Football Playoff agreement
cards.teaser: Kirby Smart raised the possibility of SEC secession if playoff expansion negotiations break down.
cards.body:
Georgia coach Kirby Smart suggested at spring meetings that the SEC could essentially leave the NCAA if no agreement is reached on the College Football Playoff. His remarks Tuesday came amid ongoing discussions about conference expansion and raised significant questions about college football's future structure.

Smart's comments represent the most dramatic statement yet about how far conferences might go to pursue their interests regarding playoff format and revenue distribution.

cards.headline: Former Iowa State star Milan Momcilovic withdraws from NBA draft, returns to college
cards.teaser: The top transfer portal player will play college basketball next season instead of turning professional.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, the top-rated player in the transfer portal, is withdrawing from the NBA draft and will play college basketball next season, his agents told ESPN. The former Iowa State forward had been evaluating his professional options.

Momcilovic's decision makes him the most sought-after player available in the transfer portal. His return to college basketball will trigger a recruiting battle among programs seeking to add the talented forward to their rosters.

cards.headline: Spielberg opposes AI in creative filmmaking decisions
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg said he does not want artificial intelligence taking over the creative process in Hollywood during an appearance on the IMO podcast hosted by Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson.

The director said AI could be useful for solving medical issues but should not replace human creativity in film. He drew a line at using AI as the final word on anything creative.

Spielberg did not elaborate on specific AI applications he finds acceptable or problematic in filmmaking. The comments come as the entertainment industry grapples with how to use AI tools while protecting creative jobs and artistic control.

The director is among the most successful filmmakers in Hollywood history, with credits including Jaws, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Schindler's List, and Saving Private Ryan. His position carries weight as studios and production companies explore AI for script analysis, visual effects, and other filmmaking tasks.

No major studios have announced plans to use AI for final creative decisions on films. However, AI tools are increasingly used in pre-production, post-production, and marketing.

Spielberg's remarks reflect broader concerns in Hollywood about AI's role in entertainment. Writers and actors went on strike in 2023 in part over AI protections. Those strikes resulted in contract language limiting how studios can use AI to replace human work.

The director did not say whether he has used AI tools in any capacity on his own productions. He also did not specify which medical applications of AI he considers beneficial.

His appearance on the podcast covered multiple topics beyond AI. Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson, who are siblings, launched the podcast to discuss current issues with guests from various fields.

cards.headline: Court allows Palestinian activist to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A federal appeals panel ruled pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil can stay out of custody while petitioning the Supreme Court.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel ruled Tuesday that pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil may remain free while pursuing his Supreme Court appeal. The three judges—Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman, and Thomas Hardiman—issued the order allowing Khalil to stay out of custody during the petition process.

Khalil is challenging actions taken by the Trump administration. The three-judge panel included jurists appointed by Presidents Trump, George W. Bush, and Joe Biden.

cards.headline: Senator Kim responds to Homeland Security chief over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: Democratic Senator Andy Kim pushed back after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized him for attending a protest at a New Jersey migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Senator Andy Kim of New Jersey pushed back against Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Wednesday following criticism over his attendance at a protest outside a migrant detention facility. Mullin had raised the incident during a Cabinet meeting at the White House, bringing up that Kim was struck by pepper ball spray at the demonstration.

Kim rejected the characterization that the matter was personal. His response came after he participated in demonstrations outside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility located in his state.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans endorse Paxton after Texas primary
cards.teaser: Senate Republican leaders moved to repair relations with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his primary victory over Senator John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are working to repair their relationship with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following a contentious primary battle. Senate Majority Leader John Thune phoned Paxton on Wednesday and subsequently endorsed him on a radio show, signaling party unity ahead of the general election.

Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn in a competitive $130 million Republican primary. As Republicans seek to maintain their Senate majority, they are emphasizing to major donors that controlling the chamber depends heavily on winning in Texas. The outreach aims to move past the divisive primary and focus on the general election challenge ahead.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Thought Her Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady described being frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened while watching her husband's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. She said she thought he might have suffered a stroke during the event.

The former first lady described being shocked by Joe Biden's faltering performance, saying she had never seen him perform that way before or since. Her remarks came in an interview set to air on Sunday.

cards.headline: FIFA Faces Investigation Over World Cup Ticket Pricing
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey authorities are investigating FIFA over alleged misleading ticket sales practices.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's 2026 World Cup ticket sales practices. The probe was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket sales and seat locations.

Investigators are examining whether FIFA provided accurate information to consumers during the ticket purchasing process. The inquiry focuses on the association's pricing and sales practices.

cards.headline: Space Stocks Rise Sharply Ahead of SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile shares surged as investors anticipate the SpaceX public offering.
cards.body:
Shares of space industry companies including Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile jumped in trading, with some observers drawing parallels to previous bubbles in electric vehicle stocks. The rally comes as SpaceX prepares for its initial public offering.

Analysts have begun evaluating how the SpaceX IPO will compare to previous large market debuts. The offering is expected to be among the largest in recent years for a private space company.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: A NASA spacecraft photographed Mars in high resolution while passing the planet on its way to study a distant asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed views of Mars during a flyby of the red planet. The probe took high-resolution images, including views of Mars' south pole, as it used the planet's gravity to assist its trajectory toward its ultimate destination.

Psyche is on a mission to study a metal-rich asteroid located in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. The spacecraft used the Mars flyby as a gravity assist maneuver while simultaneously gathering scientific imagery of the planet's surface and features.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI tools
cards.teaser: Medical technology company Triomics secured $22 million in Series B funding to develop artificial intelligence systems designed specifically for oncology.
cards.body:
Triomics closed a $22 million Series B funding round led by Battery Ventures. The company develops artificial intelligence tools designed specifically for cancer treatment centers and oncology practices.

The funding will support the development and deployment of oncology-focused AI systems at cancer centers, helping address the unique workflows and challenges of cancer care facilities.

cards.headline: Arizona forward Koa Peat keeps name in NBA draft
cards.teaser: The projected first-round pick decided to remain in the draft pool rather than return to college.
cards.body: Arizona forward Koa Peat is staying in the NBA draft, according to sources who spoke with ESPN on Wednesday. The projected first-round pick has decided to forgo his remaining college eligibility with the Wildcats to pursue his professional career.

cards.headline: Horror film Obsession sees rare box office increase in second weekend
cards.teaser: The film made history with a second-weekend spike in ticket sales, a pattern not seen since Sound of Freedom.
cards.body:
Obsession has achieved a notable box office milestone by growing its earnings during its second weekend in release, establishing itself as this summer's breakout hit. The horror film joins an exclusive group of recent releases to accomplish this feat, with Sound of Freedom being the last film to experience a similar second-weekend spike.

The production has drawn particular attention for its cinematography, which industry observers have highlighted as a standout element of the film.

cards.headline: ABC World News Tonight wins fourth consecutive Emmy for live news program
cards.teaser: ABC News took eight awards at the 47th annual News Emmys, while National Geographic won seven.
cards.body:
ABC World News Tonight With David Muir won the outstanding live news program Emmy for the fourth consecutive year at the 47th annual News Emmys. ABC News led all networks with eight total awards at the ceremony.

National Geographic earned seven News Emmys, with much of that success coming from the series Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. Both ABC and National Geographic are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Morris Day says he will not perform at National Mall celebration despite being listed
cards.teaser: The singer denied what he called rumors he would headline the Freedom 250 concert, though organizers announced him for the June 27 show.
cards.body:
Morris Day and the Time will not perform at the Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall, according to the musician. Despite event organizers listing him as a headliner for the celebration of the nation's 250th birthday, Day denied the announcement and told fans the appearance is off.

The Great American State Fair is planned as a 16-day patriotic celebration in Washington. Other artists announced for the event include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, Vanilla Ice, the Commodores, C+C Music Factory, and Milli Vanilli.

cards.headline: Student calls out CBS News while accepting Mike Wallace scholarship at Emmys
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos said the recent direction of CBS News stains the legacy of Mike Wallace during his acceptance speech.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School, criticized CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmys. The student journalist from Washington said the outlet's recent direction stains the legacy of the CBS reporter for whom the award is named.

Scott Pelley, a former CBS Evening News anchor, presented the scholarship. The award is named after Mike Wallace, a longtime CBS journalist.

cards.headline: BBC analysis examines thousands of Trump social media posts
cards.teaser: The network's journalists reviewed the president's posting patterns and content.
cards.body:
BBC journalists Ros Atkins and the BBC Verify team analysed thousands of posts made by President Trump on social media, examining patterns and themes in his online communications.

The review systematically investigated Trump's digital messaging strategy and the topics he prioritizes when communicating directly with the public through social media platforms.

cards.headline: Nintendo adds Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online service next week
cards.teaser: Nintendo announced it will add Donkey Kong 64 to its Switch Online subscription service on June 3.
cards.body:
Nintendo is expanding its Nintendo 64 game library on Switch Online with the addition of Donkey Kong 64. The game will become available to subscribers of the Switch Online Expansion Pack tier on June 3.

Donkey Kong 64 originally released for the Nintendo 64 console in the late 1990s. The game joins a growing collection of N64 titles that Nintendo has made available to subscribers through its premium online service.

cards.headline: Leonora Carrington painting from psychiatric confinement to be shown publicly for first time
cards.teaser: A work created by the artist during her time in psychiatric care will go on display.
cards.body:
A painting created by surrealist artist and writer Leonora Carrington during her time in a psychiatric facility will be publicly exhibited for the first time. The work has remained unseen by the public until now.

The Guardian reported on the upcoming exhibition of this significant artwork from Carrington's history.

cards.headline: Kanye West label head sues to identify person behind defamatory websites
cards.teaser: Larry Jackson asked a judge to unmask an anonymous figure he says is trying to destroy him with reputational warfare.
cards.body:
Larry Jackson, who runs a label associated with Kanye West, filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous person. Jackson claims the individual is behind websites that defame him.

Jackson described the campaign as reputational warfare aimed at destroying him. He asked a judge to help identify the mystery figure behind the sites.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo responds to criticism of recent clothing choices
cards.teaser: The singer said she should not be responsible for some guy sexualizing her after facing backlash over recent outfits.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo addressed criticism of her recent clothing after internet commenters said her outfits both infantilized and sexualized her. The singer said she should not be held responsible for how others sexualize her.

The backlash focused on multiple recent appearances where Rodrigo wore outfits that some online critics described as inappropriate. She defended her clothing choices in response to the comments.

cards.headline: Basque Cheesecake Inventor Prepares to Retire, Says He Prefers Chocolate
cards.teaser: Santiago Rivera, who created the burnt cheesecake in the 1980s, is handing his kitchen to his children.
cards.body:
Santiago Rivera is widely credited with inventing the Basque cheesecake in the 1980s. Decades after creating the dessert that spawned countless variations worldwide, he is preparing to retire and transfer his kitchen to his children.

Rivera said he does not love the many spinoff versions of his cheesecake that have appeared over the years. Despite his fame for the burnt cheesecake, he revealed that he personally prefers chocolate.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney releases 20th solo album
cards.teaser: The musician discusses collaborating with actor Paul Mescal on his new record
cards.body:
I don't have your original card text to reference, but based on the BBC News source provided, here's a rewritten card:

Paul McCartney has released his 20th solo album, titled "The Boys of Dungeon Lane." The music legend describes the tracks as "memory songs," drawing from his personal experiences and reflections.

In a recent interview, McCartney shared an amusing anecdote about collaborating with actor Paul Mescal on guitar, joking that Mescal knew the instrument better than he did. McCartney has also expressed interest in the upcoming Beatles biopics currently in development.

cards.headline: National Trust applies fresh chalk to preserve hill figure
cards.body:
The National Trust is undertaking a maintenance project on a famous chalk figure to prevent it from deteriorating in the rain. Teams of staff and volunteers will apply 17 tonnes of fresh chalk to refresh the figure's outline.

The figure is known for its distinctive and cheeky appearance. Regular chalk applications are necessary to preserve these iconic chalk hill figures, which face ongoing erosion from weather exposure.

cards.headline: Von Miller says he lobbied Broncos coach Sean Payton for return to Denver
cards.teaser: The former Super Bowl MVP said he will play in 2026 and has already reached out to his former team.
cards.body: Von Miller confirmed Wednesday that he will definitely play for an NFL team during the 2026 season. The Super Bowl MVP has already made his pitch to Denver coach Sean Payton, expressing his interest in returning to the Broncos. Miller played a key role in Denver's Super Bowl 50 championship and is seeking another opportunity with his former team.

cards.headline: Trump remarks on Iran differ from earlier optimism about deal
cards.teaser: President Trump's comments during a Cabinet meeting contrasted with his weekend statements suggesting an agreement with Iran was near.
cards.body:
President Trump's remarks at a Wednesday Cabinet meeting diverged from his recent optimistic statements about reaching a peace deal with Iran. Over the weekend, Trump had suggested an agreement to end the conflict was imminent, and markets responded positively—oil prices fell below $100 a barrel as investors grew hopeful about resolving the nearly three-month U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

However, Trump's more recent comments indicated a harder stance, describing Iran as "negotiating on fumes." The shift in tone accompanied new U.S. defensive strikes against Iranian military facilities after the downing of Iranian attack drones, according to U.S. officials.

hero.headline: US Strikes Iran Again as Fragile Ceasefire Frays
hero.body:
The United States conducted new military strikes against Iran on Wednesday, targeting attack drones and a drone ground control station in the country's south. A US official characterized the attacks as self-defense measures, marking the second round of American military action in three days.

The strikes occurred amid a month-old ceasefire that continues to show signs of instability. The military escalation threatens ongoing negotiations aimed at ending a three-month conflict between the two nations.

Iran responded to the American strikes by attacking a US airbase, according to Iranian claims. Oil prices jumped 3 percent following Iran's announcement, reflecting concerns about potential disruptions to global energy supplies.

The recent military actions complicate diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict. President Trump rejected Iran's counter-proposal to a US peace plan, calling it "totally unacceptable." The Iranian response, passed through Pakistani mediators, emphasized the necessity of lifting US sanctions, ending the American naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and guarantees against renewed attacks.

The US had presented a one-page, 14-point memorandum of understanding a week earlier. That proposal reportedly included a moratorium on Iranian nuclear enrichment lasting up to 20 years, the transfer of Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile overseas, and the dismantling of Iranian nuclear facilities.

Iran's counter-proposal suggested shorter timelines and more limited concessions. The country offered a shorter enrichment moratorium, partial export of enriched uranium, and refusal to accept facility dismantling.

Netanyahu warned that the war remains unfinished, stating that Iranian nuclear stockpiles must be removed. "It's not over, because there's still nuclear material that has to be taken out of Iran," Netanyahu told CBS, adding that the best approach would involve entering Iran to secure the fissile material as part of an agreement.

Trump indicated he had discussed potential military options with Netanyahu. He stated the US could "go in for two more weeks and do every single target," though he noted that remaining targets would constitute "final touches" to operations already underway.

The ceasefire, declared on April 8, showed renewed strain as the UAE and Kuwait reported drone incursions in their airspace. A drone attack also started a small fire on a ship off the coast in the region.

Trump downplayed some concerns about Iran's enriched uranium stockpile, suggesting that satellite surveillance through the Space Force was sufficient to monitor access. He expressed confidence that "if anybody got near the place, we will know about it and we'll blow them up."

The situation has created significant uncertainty in energy markets and raised concerns about further escalation. Trump faces pressure to maintain the ceasefire ahead of a scheduled visit to China, which has been pushing for an end to hostilities and the opening of the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan Continue Fighting Despite China Mediation Efforts
cards.teaser: Open warfare between Pakistan and Afghanistan has continued for months with no resolution in sight.
cards.body:
Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan months ago, and neither country appears ready to end hostilities. China has attempted to mediate between the two nations but has not succeeded in brokering peace.

The conflict has extended well beyond initial expectations. Both Pakistan and Afghanistan have maintained their military postures despite diplomatic pressure from regional powers to stand down.

cards.headline: Israel Orders Mass Evacuations in Southern Lebanon as Fighting Intensifies
cards.teaser: Israeli military told residents of large areas of southern Lebanon to leave their homes.
cards.body:
Israel has declared large areas of southern Lebanon south of the Zahrani River as "combat zones" and issued evacuation orders for residents. The military has threatened fresh strikes against Hezbollah as fighting intensifies in the region.

The escalation marks a significant expansion of the conflict in southern Lebanon, with Israeli forces intensifying operations against the militant group.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo Over Ebola Outbreak
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola cases spread.
cards.body:
Uganda has closed its border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo following an Ebola outbreak in the region. Seven confirmed cases have been reported in Kampala, Uganda's capital, prompting the government to take preventive measures to contain the virus's spread.

The World Health Organization's director-general has called for an immediate ceasefire in eastern Congo, warning of a "catastrophic collision of disease and conflict" as the Ebola outbreak in Ituri province outpaces response efforts. Uganda's disease surveillance systems are being mobilized to manage the situation, while international airlines have been urged to implement safety protocols similar to those used during the COVID pandemic.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Partial Internet Access After 88 Days of Near-Total Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government is allowing some people to reconnect with the world after months offline.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access after maintaining a near-total shutdown for 88 days that blocked television, chat services, and online news. The move comes as the country navigates a fragile ceasefire with the US during ongoing negotiations to end a three-month conflict.

The reconnection remains incomplete and uncertain. Not all Iranians have regained access, and those who have worry about how long the restored service will continue, given the government's track record of cutting communications.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Thought Her Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady described being frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened while watching her husband's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. She said she thought he might have suffered a stroke during the event.

The former first lady described being shocked by Joe Biden's faltering performance, saying she had never seen him perform that way before or since. Her remarks came in an interview set to air on Sunday.

cards.headline: Basque Cheesecake Inventor Prepares to Retire, Says He Prefers Chocolate
cards.teaser: Santiago Rivera, who created the burnt cheesecake in the 1980s, is handing his kitchen to his children.

Santiago Rivera is widely credited with inventing the Basque cheesecake in the 1980s. Decades after creating the dessert that spawned countless variations worldwide, he is preparing to retire and transfer his kitchen to his children.

hero.headline: At least 2 dead, 9 missing after chemical tank implosion at Washington state paper mill
hero.body:
At least two people are dead and nine workers remain unrecovered after a chemical tank implosion at a paper mill in Longview, Washington.

The disaster involved white liquor, a caustic chemical used in paper production. Contaminated water from the implosion is being flushed through Longview's ditch system as part of the response effort.

Washington's governor said the incident could be the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history. The statement underscores the severity of the accident at the facility.

Emergency responders are working to locate the nine workers who remain unaccounted for. The implosion occurred at a tank containing the chemical solution, which is part of the paper manufacturing process.

White liquor is a mixture of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide dissolved in water. The substance is highly alkaline and used to break down wood chips into pulp during papermaking. Contact with the chemical can cause severe burns and other injuries.

Authorities have not disclosed what caused the tank to implode or the full extent of injuries to workers at the scene. The paper mill is a major employer in the Longview area.

The contaminated water cleanup effort involves directing the chemical-laden runoff through existing drainage infrastructure. Officials have not provided details on environmental impacts or risks to nearby waterways.

Search and recovery operations continue for the nine missing workers. The two confirmed deaths add to what is already one of the most serious workplace accidents in recent Washington state history.

The facility remains closed as investigators work to determine the cause of the implosion and assess damage to the tank and surrounding structures.

cards.headline: U.S. conducts second strike on Iran in three days
cards.teaser: American forces hit a drone launch site in Iran as negotiations to end the three-month conflict continue.
cards.body:
The United States conducted defensive strikes against an Iranian military facility after downing Iranian attack drones, according to U.S. officials. This marks the second American military action against Iran in three days.

The strikes occur amid a fragile ceasefire and ongoing negotiations to end the three-month conflict between the two nations. President Trump continues to maintain maximum demands on Iran as talks remain stalled. Oil prices have risen following the military action amid concerns about potential disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Prosecutors say the ex-agency official stole approximately 300 gold bars from the CIA.
cards.body:
Federal authorities arrested David Rush, a former CIA official, after discovering $40 million worth of gold bars in his home. The FBI executed the arrest following the discovery of the precious metals.

Prosecutors allege Rush stole the gold from the CIA during his time with the agency. Court documents indicate the former officer is accused of defrauding the government by lying about his credentials. Sources say approximately 300 gold bars were recovered from his residence. The case involves one of the largest thefts from a U.S. intelligence agency in recent memory.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Ken Paxton after Texas Senate primary
cards.teaser: Party leaders are working with the Texas attorney general following a contentious primary race.
cards.body:
Republican officials have begun reconciling with Ken Paxton following his victory in the Texas Senate primary runoff. The move marks a shift in party dynamics after the contentious contest.

Democrat James Talarico will face Paxton in the general election. Talarico's campaign has pivoted from his primary messaging to focus on attacking Paxton's scandals and controversies as the central strategy for the November matchup.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over Polymarket insider trading
cards.teaser: A Google staffer allegedly used insider information to profit $1.2 million on the prediction market platform.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice filed criminal charges against a Google engineer who allegedly used insider information to trade on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The employee made $1.2 million in profits from wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, risking over $2.7 million in the process.

This marks the second known federal prosecution for insider trading on a prediction market site, signaling heightened government attention to trading activity on these platforms. Polymarket allows users to bet on the outcomes of political, economic, and cultural events.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought husband was having a stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady described being frightened by Joe Biden's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and feared he might have suffered a stroke.

The debate became a pivotal moment in the 2024 campaign, raising widespread questions about Biden's fitness for office. Her comments, shared in an interview set to air on Sunday, offer insight into the family's private concerns during this significant political event.

cards.teaser: The network's journalists reviewed the president's posting patterns and content.

BBC journalists Ros Atkins and the BBC Verify team analysed thousands of posts made by President Trump on social media, examining patterns and themes in his online communications.

hero.headline: Google Engineer Charged With Insider Trading on Polymarket Bets
hero.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged a Google employee with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential company information to make $1.2 million on prediction market bets.

The engineer, identified as Michele Spagnuolo, worked at Google and allegedly accessed nonpublic data about search trends through his position. He then used that information to place wagers on Polymarket, a platform where users bet on real-world events including political outcomes, economic indicators, and other measurable occurrences.

According to the unsealed complaint, Spagnuolo placed bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign and risked more than $2.7 million on the wagers. Prosecutors say he knew the outcome of these bets before the general public because he had accessed Google's confidential information about search-related trends.

The charges represent a notable application of insider trading law to prediction markets. While insider trading statutes traditionally apply to securities markets, federal authorities argue the same legal principles extend to any market where nonpublic information provides an unfair advantage. The case marks only the second known instance of the federal government filing criminal charges against someone for allegedly using insider information to profit on a prediction market platform.

Search trend data represents particularly valuable information because it can reveal shifting public interest before it becomes widely known. Spagnuolo's access to Google's internal systems gave him an advantage unavailable to other bettors on Polymarket.

Prediction markets like Polymarket have grown in popularity as a forecasting tool based on collective predictions. Users can profit when their predictions prove correct. The platform has gained attention recently for allowing bets on various high-stakes events, raising concerns about potential misuse of classified or confidential information.

The $1.2 million in alleged profits suggests Spagnuolo made multiple successful bets over a period of time. Prosecutors have not disclosed which specific events or search trends the bets covered or the duration of the alleged scheme.

Insider trading charges carry potential prison sentences and substantial financial penalties. The defendant faces prosecution under federal laws designed to ensure fair markets by preventing individuals with privileged access to information from exploiting it for personal gain.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges. The company employs thousands of engineers who have access to various types of internal data as part of their regular work responsibilities. The case highlights the challenges companies face in monitoring employees' personal financial activities, particularly as prediction markets and cryptocurrency-based betting platforms continue to expand.

cards.headline: China's Pork Prices Hit 16-Year Low as Consumer Spending Weakens
cards.teaser: Pork prices in China, a key inflation measure, reached their lowest level in 16 years.
cards.body:
Pork prices in China have fallen to their lowest level in 16 years, reflecting weak consumer demand and excessive hog production. As a key inflation indicator in China, the decline signals economic strain on households that are spending less.

The price drop underscores broader pressures in the Chinese economy, where consumers are tightening their budgets while hog farmers face oversupply challenges in the sector.

cards.headline: Australia Sues 3M for $2 Billion Over Contamination at Defense Sites
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed a $2 billion lawsuit against US manufacturer 3M over chemical contamination.
cards.body:
Australia has launched its largest-ever government lawsuit against 3M, demanding A$2 billion in damages over contamination at defence sites. The case centers on "forever chemicals" present in firefighting foam used across 28 military installations.

These persistent substances contaminate both the environment and the human body. The Australian government is seeking to recover costs associated with the cleanup and remediation of affected defence bases.

cards.headline: China Expands Factory Network Overseas as Trade Surplus Grows
cards.teaser: China is building manufacturing facilities around the world as its trade surplus continues to expand.
cards.body:
Chinese companies are establishing factories in countries across the globe, a move that has raised concerns among local competitors. The expansion comes as China's trade surplus has grown to $1.2 trillion.

The factory exports represent a shift in how China engages with global trade. Rather than only shipping finished goods, Chinese manufacturers are now setting up production facilities in foreign markets.

cards.headline: FIFA Faces Investigation Over World Cup Ticket Pricing
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey authorities are investigating FIFA over alleged misleading ticket sales practices.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's 2026 World Cup ticket sales practices. The probe was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket sales and seat locations.

Investigators are examining whether FIFA provided accurate information to consumers during the ticket purchasing process. The inquiry focuses on the association's pricing and sales practices.

cards.headline: Ferrari's First Electric Car Meets Resistance in Italy and Beyond
cards.teaser: Ferrari's debut electric vehicle faced criticism online and skepticism from analysts following its release.
cards.body:
Ferrari unveiled its new Luce electric model, prompting significant backlash. The vehicle sparked mockery on social media and divided public opinion, while investors responded by selling shares in the Italian automaker.

A former Ferrari chairman warned that the electric car could destroy the brand's legacy. The criticism reflects deeper concerns about whether an electric vehicle aligns with Ferrari's identity as a manufacturer of high-performance combustion engine sports cars.

cards.headline: Global Automakers Struggle to Match China's Electric Vehicle Dominance
cards.teaser: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers have built control over the supply chains shaping the global auto industry.
cards.body:
Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers have established dominant positions across the global automotive supply chain. The BBC's factory visits in China documented how domestic EV producers control critical segments of the industry, including battery production, raw materials processing, and manufacturing infrastructure that international automakers depend on for their own electric vehicle development.

This control over key ecosystem components gives Chinese producers a significant competitive advantage in shaping the future of the global auto industry.

cards.headline: Space Stocks Rise Sharply Ahead of SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile shares surged as investors anticipate the SpaceX public offering.
cards.body:
Shares of space industry companies including Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile jumped in trading, with some observers drawing parallels to previous bubbles in electric vehicle stocks. The rally comes as SpaceX prepares for its initial public offering.

Analysts have begun evaluating how the SpaceX IPO will compare to previous large market debuts. The offering is expected to be among the largest in recent years for a private space company.

hero.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination from firefighting foam
hero.body:
The Australian government filed a lawsuit against American manufacturing giant 3M over contamination from chemicals used in firefighting foam at defense sites across the country. The case seeks A$2 billion in damages and represents the largest legal action ever brought by the Australian government.

The lawsuit centers on contamination caused by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly known as PFAS or forever chemicals, which were used in firefighting foam at military installations. These synthetic chemicals earned their nickname because they do not break down naturally in the environment and can persist for thousands of years.

3M, a multinational conglomerate headquartered in Minnesota, manufactured the firefighting foam products that contained these chemicals. The foam was widely used at defense facilities for its effectiveness in suppressing fuel fires.

PFAS chemicals have raised health and environmental concerns globally because they accumulate in soil, water, and human bodies over time. Scientists have linked exposure to these substances with various health problems, though the Australian government has not specified the extent of contamination at the affected defense sites or the number of locations involved.

The Australian legal action follows similar lawsuits against 3M in other countries. In the United States, 3M agreed to pay more than $10 billion to settle claims related to PFAS contamination of public water systems. The company also faced litigation over contamination at military bases and airports where the firefighting foam was used.

3M stopped manufacturing PFAS-based firefighting foam in 2002 and announced in 2022 that it would phase out all PFAS production by the end of 2025. However, the legacy contamination from decades of use remains a persistent problem at sites around the world.

The Australian case marks an escalation in government efforts to hold manufacturers accountable for environmental damage from forever chemicals. The A$2 billion figure reflects the scale of cleanup costs and potential remediation required at contaminated defense installations.

Neither 3M nor Australian government officials provided additional details about which specific defense sites are affected or the timeline for legal proceedings.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California civil rights agency won a legal victory against Tesla as the court denied the company's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination case.
cards.body:
A California court rejected Tesla's motion to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency. The ruling allows the case to proceed to trial, which is expected to begin in July.

The California Civil Rights Department celebrated the court's decision as a significant victory in its legal action against Tesla over allegations of racial discrimination at the company's facilities.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 electric SUVs
cards.teaser: Electric vehicle maker Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of its R2 SUV. CEO RJ Scaringe called it "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date."

The R2 marks Rivian's expansion into a more affordable segment of the electric SUV market, complementing its existing R1T truck and R1S SUV lineup.

cards.headline: Google's artificial intelligence struggles with basic spelling tasks
cards.teaser: Google's AI systems are having difficulty spelling common words, including the company's own name, in a persistent technical problem.
cards.body:
Google is facing criticism over spelling errors in its artificial intelligence systems. The company's AI has struggled to correctly spell common words, including "Google" itself, as well as instruction words like "disregard," "stop," and "ignore." These spelling failures have been widely reported across Google's AI search features and language models.

The issues come as Google has made AI-generated answers central to its search experience. This shift represents a significant change for SEO strategies that previously relied on traditional search results, with brands now having limited visibility into how Google's AI describes them to users.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: A NASA spacecraft photographed Mars in high resolution while passing the planet on its way to study a distant asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed views of Mars during a flyby of the red planet. The probe took high-resolution images, including views of Mars' south pole, as it used the planet's gravity to assist its trajectory toward its ultimate destination.

Psyche is on a mission to study a metal-rich asteroid located in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. The spacecraft used the Mars flyby as a gravity assist maneuver while simultaneously gathering scientific imagery of the planet's surface and features.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI tools
cards.teaser: Medical technology company Triomics secured $22 million in Series B funding to develop artificial intelligence systems designed specifically for oncology.
cards.body:
Triomics closed a $22 million Series B funding round led by Battery Ventures. The company develops artificial intelligence tools designed specifically for cancer treatment centers and oncology practices.

The funding will support the development and deployment of oncology-focused AI systems at cancer centers, helping address the unique workflows and challenges of cancer care facilities.

cards.headline: Nintendo adds Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online service next week
